title: Active noise suppression and reservation rightsizing roadmap
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Summary: After the 2026-02-09 capacity incident affecting two Dedicated clusters, we observed a class of noisy tenant behaviour that bypassed existing reservation heuristics and triggered evictions and degraded SLAs. This ticket defines a concise operational roadmap for: (1) fast detection and active suppression of noisy tenants via signal fingerprinting, (2) automated reservation rightsizing that adjusts fractional reservations at 1-5 minute intervals, and (3) burst policy tuning to prevent sustained eviction storms while preserving short tail latency.

Context and root cause hypothesis:
- Incident showed sustained KV cache churn + long prompt sequences from a small subset of tenants which caused eviction cascades and starvation of queued requests.
- Existing burst tokenbucket allowed long bursts to consume shared pool; tenant soft-resize logic did not react quickly enough due to 10m reconciliation window.
- Telemetry lacked a stable "noise signature" that combined: sequence-length histogram shift, cache miss-rate spike, and inter-arrival jitter.

Goals:
- Detect noisy tenants within 60s of onset with <2% false positive rate.
- Contain noisy tenants using a lightweight active-suppression policy (temporary hardened cgroup + 2x charge-back) without full eviction.
- Rightsize reservations automatically for affected tenants within 5 minutes, reducing eviction rate by >= 70% in repeat scenarios.
- Tune global burst policy to prioritize short tail latency for high-SLA customers while allowing controlled short bursts for best-effort tenants.

Workstreams and deliverables:
1) Telemetry & Detection (owner: Liam Chen)
   - Implement a composite noise signature: sequence-length percentile shift + KV cache miss delta + request burstiness score.
   - New metric series: tenant.noise_score (0..1), tenant.seq95, tenant.kv_miss_delta.
   - Add anomaly detector in telemetry pipeline (Spark job -> metrics service) and a lightweight on-host classifier for <60s detection.
   - Deliverable: confluence doc + dashboard (link below) + alert rule.

2) Active suppression primitives (owner: Priya Anand)
   - Implement temporary tenant throttling mode: reduce burst bucket refill to 20% and enforce per-tenant cpu/gpu share floor.
   - Introduce a soft-isolation cgroup mode that isolates noisy workloads onto a low-priority QoS lane rather than evicting.
   - Deliverable: PR with kernel-safe cgroup changes, rollout plan, smoke test suite.

3) Reservation rightsizer (owner: Noah Patel)
   - Build an autoscaler that adjusts fractional reservations at 1/5/10 minute lookbacks using EWMA of historical token consumption vs requested throughput.
   - Ensure rightsizer respects tenant SLAs and change-rate limits (max 20% resize per minute).
   - Deliverable: service + API, simulation harness, and a canary for 10 tenants.

4) Burst-policy tuning & fairness (owner: Systems SRE)
   - Redefine global burst policy to have two lanes: short-burst (<=30s) for interactive tenants and long-burst capped for best-effort.
   - Introduce per-tenant burst credits decay to avoid sustained long bursts.
   - Deliverable: updated policy, load-test results, rollout gates.

5) Runbook & Playbook updates (owner: On-call team)
   - Update postmortem runbook with new detection/mitigation steps, Slack runbook automation shortcuts, and escalation matrix.

Success criteria and metrics:
- mean eviction rate per cluster during repeats decreases by >=70% in testbed.
- MTTR for noisy-tenant events reduced from 45m to <=10m.
- No customer SLA regressions in canary (0 critical incidents during 7-day canary).
- Noise_score precision >=98% in held-out historical simulation.

Rollout plan and risks:
- Phase 0 (lab): telemetry + simulation (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (internal canary): rightsizer + suppression on 10 non-critical tenants (1 week).
- Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 30% of clusters, monitor key metrics (2–3 weeks).
- Phase 3 (GA): enable default for all Dedicated clusters with opt-out for enterprise customers (2 weeks).
Risks: false positives causing perf degradation for legitimate bursty customers; regression in KV cache behaviour due to unintended side-effects of suppression; complexity of cross-service rollout. Mitigation: manual opt-out, automatic rollback triggers, conservative canary gates.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer a short, host-local detector for detection speed; telemetry-based detector will provide higher fidelity but with higher latency. We'll run both in tandem and require both to fire before strong suppression.
- Rightsizer decision window chosen as trade between noise vs responsiveness; smaller windows reduce latency but increase oscillation risk — we will use EWMA smoothing and change-rate limits.
- Burst policy will favor interactive tenants (by SLA tag) so some best-effort workloads may see lower peak throughput temporarily.

Artifacts and links: 
- Incident postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-09-dedicated-capacity-spike
- Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd-noise-signatures/tenant-noise-overview
- Rightsizer simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rightsizer/tree/feat/autoscale-v2
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321 (suppression cgroup)
- Load test results (internal bucket): gs://redwood-loadtests/noise-sim-2026-02

Open questions: 
- Should suppression be sticky (X minutes) or adaptive until noise_score decays to baseline? (proposal: adaptive with min 1m, max 30m).
- How aggressive should the rightsizer be for enterprise customers with committed reservations? (proposal: do not shrink below 80% of committed reservation unless manual review).

Next steps (short-term):
- Liam: land telemetry metrics and alert (ETA 2026-02-25).
- Priya: prototype suppression cgroup PR + smoke tests (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Noah: start rightsizer simulation with historical traces (ETA 2026-03-03).
- SRE: prepare canary cluster and rollback automation (ETA 2026-03-08).
